title: Overlapping boost detectors produce duplicate IDs and reject a valid replay

location.quote:
id: format!("{match_id}:{category}:{player_id}:{start:.3}"),
        player_id: Some(player_id.to_string()),
        team: None,

problem: Both segment types use the same category/player/start identifier. A player holding boost above 2200 with less than 10 boost for five seconds creates two equal IDs; validate_analysis rejects the whole replay.
trigger_or_repro: review_validate_duplicate_events_fails_but_control_is_valid drives native Collector::process_frame snapshots for 6 seconds; change boost 0 to 33 as control.
expected_vs_actual: Low boost case returns Analysis event references or time invalid; otherwise identical 33-boost case passes.
recommendation: Give event types stable distinct identifiers, separate category from detector kind, and test simultaneous detectors.
validation: Actively disproved alternate cause: same collector snapshots with boost 33 instead of 0 validate successfully. Overlap control produces exactly two different titles with identical IDs; failure persists at finish_replay and regular flush.

title: Low-boost event duration includes time while the player is absent
problem: Accumulator segments are flushed only for currently present cars. When a player disappears, the outstanding low-boost/boost segment survives; returning or EOF closes it at the later replay time, asserting an unobserved interval.
trigger_or_repro: review_absent_player_extends_observed_low_boost_event: six seconds low boost, six seconds with no car, then reappear.
expected_vs_actual: Actual observed low-boost duration is 6 s; event is 0..12 and description says boost stayed below 10 continuously.
recommendation: Flush or suspend segments when a player leaves the observable set, using last observed endpoint. Record an explicit missing-state interval.
validation: Native process_frame synthetic snapshots prove six seconds absent without increasing tracked_seconds. The event still extends to 12. No missing-data interpolation in the fixture or helper; current car set is empty during absence.

title: Defensive-exposure event spans a timing gap that metrics explicitly exclude
problem: When continuity fails, exposure is closed at the current time rather than the last continuous observation. A long skipped gap becomes part of a claimed observed exposure window.
trigger_or_repro: review_exposure_event_spans_dropped_timing_gap: 1.2 seconds with two upfield defenders, next snapshot at 5 seconds.
expected_vs_actual: Event is 0..5 although live_seconds is 1.2 and gap 1.2..5 is rejected.
recommendation: Close exposure at previous continuous frame; clear exposure before processing discontinuities; test gap/goal/reset endpoints.
validation: Active disproof attempt: test verifies live_seconds remains 1.2, proving the interval is excluded by the metric but included by event construction. Both team players are present and correctly assigned.

title: Player movement and resource baselines omit the kickoff approach
problem: The shared live flag excludes all kickoff movement before first ball contact, beyond the countdown excluded by metric copy. Boost spent accelerating to kickoff and delayed/fake kickoff motion are absent from headline averages and measured active play.
trigger_or_repro: review_kickoff_time_not_in_active_play; two seconds moving at 2250 with no first contact.
expected_vs_actual: Zero tracked seconds and no boost/speed accumulation until after the first hit; copy says excludes countdown and goal celebration without naming kickoff approach.
recommendation: Capture a gameplay phase enum and separate match/player-motion eligibility from ball-position eligibility. Document baseline semantics and create a kickoff report.

title: Dropped observation gaps have no quantified quality or exclusion summary
problem: Gaps are marked as render discontinuities and silently removed from accumulation. Coverage cannot show gap count/seconds, excluded kickoff/goal time, per-player absence, or coverage ratio, so consumers cannot assess comparability.
trigger_or_repro: review_gap_is_excluded_without_quality_accounting; 0.4-second gap in a short synthetic replay.
expected_vs_actual: live_seconds excludes the gap but no coverage field explains how much was discarded.
recommendation: Publish per-phase/per-metric observed and excluded durations with reason codes; require a coverage threshold for comparisons.

title: Several metric sample counts describe all car frames, not valid observations

location.quote:
a.samples,
                "measured",
                "Observed active-play duration with available car state; excludes countdown and goal celebration.",

problem: avg_speed and position metrics use a.samples even when velocity, team or ball is missing. The viewer tooltip prints sample_count as evidence, overstating supporting samples.
trigger_or_repro: review_partial_velocity_overstates_metric_sample_count: 100 car samples with only one valid velocity.
expected_vs_actual: avg_speed reports 100 samples but denominator is 0.1 s from a single observation.
recommendation: Track valid sample counts separately for each sufficient-statistic denominator; show coverage duration as the main support.

title: Analysis validator omits sufficient statistics and coverage integrity
problem: Validator only checks metric player reference and value finiteness. Infinite numerator, negative denominator, inconsistent ratio, and NaN/live time beyond duration are accepted.
trigger_or_repro: review_validator_accepts_corrupt_sufficient_statistics_and_coverage.
expected_vs_actual: validate_analysis accepts negative denominator, infinite numerator and NaN coverage simultaneously.
recommendation: Validate all numeric fields and nonnegative denominators; verify ratio/value consistency with tolerance and observed-time bounds.

title: Analysis validator accepts impossible metric ranges and inconsistent shot attribution
problem: Finite values alone allow negative scores, negative boost percentages, absurd sample indices and shot team disagreeing with the player. summary.players and recorder identity are not cross-checked against canonical players.
trigger_or_repro: review_validator_accepts_negative_counts_and_wrong_shot_team sets score/boost -100, shot on opponent team, frame usize::MAX.
expected_vs_actual: The validator accepts all constructed contradictions.
recommendation: Add typed range validation by metric key, canonical participant consistency, recorder membership, and frame/index bounds.

title: Duration is the last replay timestamp and includes non-gameplay time

location.quote:
duration_seconds: f64::from(last),
        blue_score,
        orange_score,

problem: Replay elapsed end time is shown as Duration in Overview/Replays. It can include pre-game countdown, goal celebrations and end sequence, and does not subtract first frame time.
trigger_or_repro: Inspect summary builder and Overview.tsx:200, Replays.tsx:416.
expected_vs_actual: A replay ending at t=360 is displayed as 6:00 even if measured active play is 300; no match-versus-replay distinction.
recommendation: Persist replay elapsed span, regulation/overtime time and observed player-motion duration separately; label them explicitly.

title: Exact supersonic state is not measured; detector prose calls threshold time supersonic
problem: Threshold accumulation is honestly named in dictionary, so missing hysteresis is not inherently wrong. The detector prose still equates >=2200 with game state, losing the 2100..2200 one-second grace interval and confusing exact state with a threshold approximation.
trigger_or_repro: Inspect >=2200 cuts and metric dictionary limitations; official v1.78 notes document hysteresis as unchanged.
expected_vs_actual: Threshold metric is valid as defined; exact state/time cannot be inferred from it, yet event calls the state supersonic.
recommendation: Keep threshold metric, change event prose to at or above 2200, or derive a separate validated state estimate with hysteresis.

title: Boost-at-speed is visually condemned despite being a neutral measurement

location.quote: Boosting at Speed

problem: Danger colour and a flame icon imply waste; parser advice still defaults to release boost without evidence about acceleration, steering or aerial purpose. The honest sentence not proven waste competes with stronger visual semantics.
trigger_or_repro: Progress Boosting at Speed card and Overview kpi-icon-wrap waste; inspect parser segment copy.
expected_vs_actual: Neutral context-dependent duration is presented as danger and among four hero KPIs.
evidence: app/src/pages/Progress.tsx:149-160; app/src/pages/Overview.tsx:129; parser supersonic segment text
recommendation: Use neutral kinematic styling; demote to descriptive stats; promote contextual pad-path/recovery opportunities once validated.

title: New threshold metrics are discarded before the product can show them
problem: get_progress exports only six legacy metric values. New threshold duration/share is computed but absent from Progress/Overview/Studio headline stats, while boost-active duration stays prominent.
trigger_or_repro: Compare EvidenceCollector::metrics with get_progress key list and ReplayStudio.tsx filter.
expected_vs_actual: Computed threshold metrics exist in replay.metrics but never reach progress row or main stat strip.
recommendation: Expose a typed stat catalog with eligibility/method/provenance, and let report needs select meaningful metrics.

title: Metric methods document gives the wrong low-boost denominator

location.quote:
| `low_boost_pct`            | Time below 10 boost          | Percentage (`%`)          | \(\frac{\text{seconds}(\text{boost} < 10.0)}{\text{tracked\_seconds}} \times 100\).                                                    | Resource measurement, not a fault determination. Pressure and starve phases can force low boost. |
| `avg_speed`                | Average speed                | Unreal units/sec (`uu/s`) | \(\frac{\int \|\vec{v}(t)\| dt}{\int dt}\) for linear velocity vectors.                                                                | Replicated velocity depends on network snapshot rates. Does not measure decision quality.        |
| `supersonic_boost_seconds` | Boosting at supersonic speed | Seconds (`s`)             | Cumulative duration where \(\|\vec{v}\| \ge 2200\text{ uu/s}\) and `boost_active == true`.                                             | Aerial direction changes and turning speed maintenance may justify brief supersonic boost.       |

problem: Documentation divides low seconds by tracked_seconds; implementation and versioned dictionary divide by valid boost seconds. Missing boost changes the numerical result.
trigger_or_repro: Compare docs row with EvidenceCollector metrics and extracted research image28.
expected_vs_actual: Docs and source disagree; code/research formula correctly exclude missing boost from denominator.
recommendation: Generate method reference from the versioned metric dictionary and remove duplicate manual formulas.

title: Duration/count aggregates have no normalized rate alternative
problem: Duration/count metrics are equal-match means, which is a valid descriptive average but not comparable behavior intensity across forfeits, overtime and different lengths. Coach receives these near time-weighted metrics without a clear unit-specific aggregation contract.
trigger_or_repro: Two matches with identical boost-at-speed rate but durations 60 and 360 seconds produce different raw-duration observations.
expected_vs_actual: Count/duration averages respond to match length; method string combines legacy weights unavailable with duration/count metrics.
recommendation: Preserve per-match means where useful, add rate/share alternatives and a typed aggregation method per metric; make completion/coverage explicit.

title: There is no metric re-derivation path for existing libraries
problem: Re-enrichment explicitly updates only capture data, never metrics/events; no source metric version upgrade/recompute operation exists. The exported functions are also absent from registered IPC.
trigger_or_repro: Search reenrich in src-tauri/src and compare apply_reenrichment SQL; existing test asserts metrics unchanged.
expected_vs_actual: New metric keys/formula fixes only reach new imports; stale libraries cannot be upgraded through the app.
recommendation: Implement immutable source replay plus versioned derivation records; offer cancellable worker-backed recomputation and rebuild dependent caches.

title: Metric dictionary does not cover scoreboard and touch metrics that the parser emits
problem: The authoritative dictionary omits goals, assists, saves, shots, score and touches, including important count semantics/heuristic confidence. It includes suspected_unnecessary_boost_s despite no producer.
trigger_or_repro: Compare parser metric keys with JSON catalog; rg suspected finds catalog only.
expected_vs_actual: A dictionary claimed authoritative cannot explain or validate several production metrics and advertises a permanently unavailable one.
recommendation: Make catalog complete and machine-check producer/consumer coverage; separate planned research metrics from produced metrics.

title: Game phase magic numbers hide exported decoder constants
problem: 53 and 67 are valid canonical subtr-actor game-state constants, but magic literals obscure meaning and create drift risk.
trigger_or_repro: Inspect dependency frame_components.rs GAME_STATE_KICKOFF_COUNTDOWN=53 and GAME_STATE_GOAL_SCORED_REPLAY=67.
expected_vs_actual: Codes are correct; source does not explain them at their use.
recommendation: Import exported named constants and phase tracker instead of duplicating phase logic.

title: Discovery and full decode disagree on metadata normalization
problem: Discovery derives mode solely from TeamSize, accepts arbitrary header IDs, omits zero-score fallback and does not always_check_crc. Full decode filters playlists and ID characters, and fills missing zero scores. Different entry points can show inconsistent identity/mode/results for the same input.
trigger_or_repro: Compare discover_replays to decode ID/mode/score paths; CLI discover versus parse.
expected_vs_actual: A nonstandard playlist with TeamSize=2 discovers as 2v2 but parses as unknown; missing 0 score remains null only in discovery.
recommendation: Create one canonical header normalization function and explicit validation level; use it across all parsing entry points.

title: Discovery silently omits every corrupt or unreadable replay
problem: Read and parser failures are silently continued; folder count reports successes only, hiding files and reasons. replay_paths also flattens directory-entry errors.
trigger_or_repro: Place unreadable/corrupt .replay beside good input; discover reports success count without errors.
expected_vs_actual: No result row for rejected inputs; users cannot distinguish no replay from decoding failure.
recommendation: Return per-file outcomes with reason and scanned/importable/rejected counts; retain bounded enumeration.

title: Match completion and roster changes are not represented in analytics eligibility
problem: ReplaySummary lacks completion/forfeit/leaver/mutator/season metadata. Analytics provenance asks for these absent keys and accepts all metric-bearing matches, making comparison cohorts unable to distinguish shortened or materially different play.
trigger_or_repro: Inspect summary type, analytics match_provenance JSON and eligibility chain.
expected_vs_actual: Short matches are included with no completion reason; source_revision cannot explain forfeits or team roster context.
recommendation: Capture available completion/playlist/mutator signals with unknown states; use explicit cohort policy rather than arbitrary 210-second rejection.

title: Collector frame-processing logic has no committed tests or golden replay oracle
problem: Original six tests cover resource arithmetic, type compatibility and validator cases, but never process_frame. No real .replay fixture or independently checked metric oracle is tracked. This allowed duplicate IDs and continuity defects to survive.
trigger_or_repro: Original cargo test -p replay-core --locked; inspect six unit tests and tracked fixture list.
expected_vs_actual: No native snapshot test drives goals, kickoffs, gaps, disappearance or overlapping detectors before this review wrapper.
recommendation: Commit synthetic ProcessorView regression tests, property tests and licensed/minimized golden replay fixtures with independently verified expected intervals.

title: Research mode cards prescribe absolute tactics and unvalidated numeric outcomes

location.quote:
short drill: Low-Risk Shadow Defense Scrimmage: Complete 3 ranked 1v1 games with an absolute rule against flipping into defensive challenges; rely entirely on driving, powerslide turns, and single-jump blocks5.  
measurable practice outcome: Zero defensive challenges that result in the player sliding past the ball into the opponent's backboard or corner1.  
match-transfer check: Empty-net counter-attack goals conceded drop to ![][image39] per match across a 5-game evaluation block1.

problem: The report calls its cards evidence-grounded but prescribes absolute no-flip ranked play, fixed midfield limits, zero kickoff goals and universal boost/recovery thresholds. It also says 36 boost enables any save. These are hypotheses, not calibrated detector or coaching facts; the repository audit deliberately rejected them.
trigger_or_repro: Read section03 plus extracted images38..54, and RESEARCH_AUDIT mode-card rejection.
expected_vs_actual: Unverified tactical heuristics are written as guarantees and target metrics; citations do not validate numeric cutoffs.
recommendation: Keep drill constraints as optional authored experiments with exceptions; support direct replay observations and expert-reviewed annotations; do not import universal targets.

title: Research over-abstention conflates no calibrated forecast with no useful comparison

location.quote:
* *Cross-Sectional Confounding*: Comparing a Diamond player's speed to an SSL player demonstrates how experts move, but provides zero information on the rate at which an individual can acquire those motor-perceptual skills1.

### **Decision: Full Abstention from Promotional Forecasting**

problem: The report overstates evidence restrictions (e.g. cross-sectional expert comparison provides zero information and strict one observation for every tactical question). Avoiding unsupported grades/forecasts is correct, but prohibits descriptive personal baselines and multi-moment explanations that can help the player.
trigger_or_repro: Read sections00/02/08 and self-critique beside prior research audit rejection of categorical impossibility.
expected_vs_actual: Research often substitutes a universal ban for bounded claim language; current product inherits long caveats instead of useful low-risk coaching.
evidence: Source inspection AntiRL Coaching Evidence Research.md:456
recommendation: Separate measured personal changes, estimated hypotheses and calibrated comparisons; permit 2–3 evidence moments supporting one priority, with optional method details.

title: Native decoded kickoff/pad/stat data is underused for practical coaching
problem: Only touch statistics are requested from the decoder graph; native pad pickups, shot geometry and controller capture exist, but report focuses on average boost/speed/half share. Kickoff outcomes, pad-pathing, recovery windows and you-versus-opponent deltas are absent from the main report.
trigger_or_repro: Compare captured pad_events/shots/controller fields to hero metrics and event detector inventory.
expected_vs_actual: High-value available facts do not create next actions; unvalidated research panels compete for attention.
recommendation: Prioritize kickoff timelines, pad-route opportunities, recovery speed and direct comparative event evidence; stage 50/50/touch-quality hypotheses behind annotated validation.
